flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No reason at all. This is the Queen's Gambit Declined move: I support d5 and open a path for the dark-square bishop. Calling it strongest and then shrugging teaches me nothing I couldn't get from a random move generator.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: d5 is the whole point of 2...e6. I am challenging c4 and claiming the center with a pawn, not vaguely 'controlling squares' like every other opening ply. If every pawn push is center-control, none of them taught me the QGD.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The dump tags this hanging, doubled_pawns, and backward_pawn. Black's d5 pawn is defended by e6 and the knight. This is the Exchange capture, not picking up a loose pawn. White's extra d-pawn is doubled only until I recapture; treating that as a reason the take is 'strongest' is inverted structure lecture.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your f6-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: It was not undefended. White's knight on c3 recaptures on d5. I did not win material; I recaptured the pawn White just took. 'Wins_material' plus 'undefended' on an equal recapture is a lie I will remember the next time the coach cries wolf.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e4 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: e4 hits the knight on d5 with tempo. That is the move. Center-control copy could have been pasted onto ply 1. Teach the kick: the knight has to move, you grab space, and you set up the big pawn center.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c3 with your d5-knight is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your queen on the white pawn and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: The discovered attack on d4 is real: the knight steps off the d-file. Nc3 does not defend d4 (knights do not cover a king-move away). You mashed two pawns together. If the 'defender' is e4, my queen is not attacking e4. Pick one idea and make it true.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c3 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Of course the knight that just captured on c3 is sitting there. Recapturing is not winning a piece. wins_material and saves_piece on a mandatory recapture is the same bug as ply 8. If you want to teach something, teach that I accept isolated-a and doubled-c pawns to keep a center.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Blank again, on the thematic break. c5 hits d4 and chips at the pawn center White just built. This is the move I needed a sentence for, and I got a verdict with no because-clause.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Reason: hanging. d4 is defended by c3 and Nf3. I am exchanging pawns in the center, not snacking on a loose one. Stop calling every capture of a defended pawn 'hanging'.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Black's queen on d8 defends d4. This is a recapture, not a free pawn. wins_material, backward_pawn, and saves_piece on 'I took back' is noise. I now distrust every 'undefended' sentence in this game.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d2 with your b4-bishop is the strongest move because it forces the king to respond.
flags.critique: The king does not have to recapture. The queen on d1 takes back, which is what happened next. 'Hanging' is also wrong: White's bishop on d2 is defended. This is a bishop trade with check, not a king hunt.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d2 with your queen is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: I recaptured out of check. Calling that wins_material because the checking piece had no extra defender is how you train me to think every trade is a tactic. king_safer is the only honest bit: I got out of check.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to e2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty strongest-move again. The bishop develops, unblocks kingside castling, and does not hang f2. Forty centipawns of 'best' with zero because-clause is a UI toast, not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a6 is playable, but moving your pawn to b6 would be better.
flags.critique: Better how? b6 prepares Bb7 and develops the light-square bishop that is still on c8. Without that, 'play a different pawn' is a stockfish whisper I cannot use in the next game.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: True that Nf6 attacked e4, but the point of pushing is to kick the knight and cramp Black, not to 'save a pawn' like I panicked. You already have kicked_by_pawn in the stack. Use it.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to d5 is the strongest move because it saves your knight from capture.
flags.critique: You tagged outpost and then lectured 'run away.' A knight on d5 in this IQP-ish structure is the dream piece: central, hard to kick, staring at c3/f4/b4. Saving it from e5 is the tactic; the outpost is the lesson. backward_pawn in the reason list is leftover garbage.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to c4 is playable, but moving your knight to g5 would be better.
flags.critique: Ng5 at what? f7? h7 with the queen? I am 1200, not a PV reader. If the alternative is the lesson, spend the because-clause on the alternative, not on a silent SAN.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b6 creates a backward pawn to defend. A better move would have been moving your pawn to h6.
flags.critique: Creates a backward pawn to defend is phrase-bank sludge: which pawn, defend against what, why do I care? h6 is dropped with no idea — luft? stop Ng5? I cannot practice a move you will not name a purpose for.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d5 with your bishop puts it where the black queen and pawn can take and you lose a knight.
flags.critique: I do not lose a knight. I trade my bishop for their knight and they recapture. Queen and pawn can take is just 'recapture exists.' The real question is why giving up that bishop (or why Ng5 instead) costs 114cp. Piece names are scrambled and the mistake is unexplained.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d5 with your queen is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended and then pin the pawn to the queen.
flags.critique: The pin of d4 to White's queen is a real idea and the first time this game almost taught a tactic. Then the sentence forgot a subject: 'and then pin the pawn' is broken English. Also the bishop is 'undefended' because White just put it there — recapture, again.

flags.quote: Moving your c1-rook to c7 is playable, but moving your queen to b4 would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: You detected rook_on_seventh and then did not say it. A rook on the seventh is one of the few positional ideas I actually want named. Qb4 pinning 'the pawn to the rook' never says b6/Rb8, so I am left guessing which pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 is playable, but taking the pawn on a4 with your b-pawn would be better because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Last move you told White a4 was hanging. This move I didn't take it, and you whisper bxa4 like a new fact. Connect them: take the pawn you just said was free. You tagged passed_pawn on b4, which is at best premature with a4 still there, and you didn't use it anyway.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to g5 is a mistake, but moving your c7-rook to c4 would be better.
flags.critique: 177cp, Lichess blunder, and I still don't know why Qg5 is bad or why R7c4 is the fix. Pin is in the reasons and never reaches the sentence. Queenside passer versus kingside sightseeing is the lesson. 'That was shaky' plus a SAN is not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to a5 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to b2 would be better because it creates a passed pawn.
flags.critique: The b-pawn is already passed on b3. b2 does not create a passer; it runs it at the rook and threatens promotion. That is the plan I needed. You used the 'creates a passed pawn' line on a push of an existing passer and skipped the promotion threat the stack already has.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your queen to h5 leaves your c7-rook hanging to the black queen.
flags.critique: The hanging-rook call is the best sentence in the dump. Framing a 1000cp drop as 'you are still worse' is cowardly: I was slightly worse, then I hung a rook. Duplicate ignored_threat in the reasons is a smell even if the copy landed.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures winning material
suggestions.detail: wins_material fires when capturedSeeCp >= 80, then move-copy says 'the X was undefended' if SEE is near the piece's value. Equal recaptures (Nxd5, bxc3, cxd4, Qxd2) all got that lie. Gate wins_material on net material versus the position before the capture sequence, or suppress it when the captured unit just moved onto the square on the previous ply. A 1200 who recaptures a pawn will not believe later 'hanging rook' warnings.

suggestions.title: Do not tag defended captures as hanging
suggestions.detail: cxd5, cxd4, and Bxd2+ all carried hanging while the target had defenders and SEE was a trade. Hanging should mean capturing it wins by SEE, not 'a capture happened.' Same bug as recapture-not-win, different reason kind. Fixing the detector removes a whole class of false tactics.

suggestions.title: Rank pawn kicks over center-control
suggestions.detail: e4 vs Nd5 and e5 vs Nf6 are kicked_by_pawn (severity 130) but copy used center_control or saves_piece. When a pawn move attacks a piece, lead with the kick and name the piece. Center-control is the generic leftover that made the first ten plies identical.

suggestions.title: Always say why the better move is better
suggestions.detail: a6→b6, Bc4→Ng5, Qg5→R7c4, and Qa5→b2 either had empty suggestedBecause or a wrong one. select-insight already computes suggestedBenefits; do not emit a SAN alternative without a because from those benefits. SkipSuggestionLecture should not apply once evalLoss is in inaccuracy range. Name the idea: develop the bishop, attack f7, stop the passer, push the passer.

suggestions.title: Surface outpost and seventh-rank over flee/save
suggestions.detail: Nd5 had outpost in reasons and copy said 'saves your knight.' Rc7 had rook_on_seventh and copy only advertised Qb4. Rank outpost / rook_on_seventh above saves_piece when both apply on a best or playable move, or concatenate: save the knight onto an outpost. Those are the positional words a club player can reuse.

suggestions.title: Add a pawn-break reason for c5/d5/e6
suggestions.detail: e6, d5, and c5 were strongest-move with empty or center_control reasons. A pawn_break / challenges_center kind when a pawn move attacks an opposing central pawn (c5xd4, d5xc4) would let templates say 'you challenge the d4-pawn' instead of silence. Fits move-effects (attacks on central squares) without an LLM.

suggestions.title: Fix chained because-clauses and pawn sludge
suggestions.detail: Qxd5 produced 'undefended and then pin the pawn to the queen' (followUp missing a subject). problem_backward_pawn 'creates a backward pawn to defend' never names which pawn. Require a noun phrase on follow-up tactics ('and it pins d4 to the queen') and make structure problems name the file. Cheap template/phrase-bank change, high eye-roll reduction.

suggestions.title: Distinguish creating a passer from pushing one
suggestions.detail: b3 correctly used 'leaves you with a passed pawn.' b2 was sold as creating a passer that already existed, and promotion was unused. If a passed_pawn already exists on that file, switch copy to 'pushes the passed pawn' and prefer promotion when the pawn reaches the 2nd/7th. Qa5's missed lesson was the promotion race, not a new passer.

whatWorked: Castling copy on plies 20 and 25 actually names king safety plus rook activation.
Nf6 (ply 26) correctly describes the discovered queen hit on d4.
Rac1 (ply 37) names the hanging a4 pawn and the Rb1 pin idea.
b3 (ply 40) and Rb1 (ply 41) teach the passer and the b-file pin without fluff.
Qh5/Qxc7 finally call the hanging rook and the take — the one tactic the rest of the game kept faking.
